To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the spatial displacement and degree of synaptic depression can develop within an input scenario of random directions and velocities by means of STDP, (b) the synaptic strength adapts such that eventually the response of the cell to the non-preferred stimulus direction becomes subthreshold, and (c) asynchronous and irregular synaptic input is required to protect the DS against stimulus noise.
the development of DS in V1 can be understood in terms of temporally asymmetric STDP and that this development is robust against noise in the input.

1) the development of the DS properties of simple cells can be explained by a combination of STDP and synaptic depression; 2) the development of DS is robust with respect to noise in the stimulus; 3) the development of direction selectivity is robust with respect the synaptic noise; 4) the degree of DS is robust against the degree of synaptic noise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether synaptic depression can account for DS of simple cells in V1.
the development of direction selectivity in the primary visual area of the mammalian brain.
the question of whether DS can emerge in a self-organized way from a random input.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DS of simple cells emerges in a self-organized manner by a combination of temporally asymmetric synaptic depression and spike-timing dependent synaptic plasticity in an unbiased input scenario.
STDP is sufficient to produce DS of simple cells, but it does not explain why it is so prevalent in the cortex.

the DS of simple cells is not the result of a prewired connection pattern, but rather a result of a learning process that is based on the interaction between the synaptic input and the cortical neuron.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

DS can emerge in an unbiased input scenario if STDP is asymmetric with respect to the temporal order of presynaptic and postsynaptic spikes and if the synaptic depression is temporally asymmetric with respect to pre- and postsynaptic activity.
the emergence of DS is not only possible but also plausible within a biologically plausible framework of STDP.
the emergence of DS in V1 simple cells is the result of the combined effect of temporally asymmetric STDP and synaptic depression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DS of simple cells in V1 can emerge from the interplay of STDP, the degree of synaptic short-term depression and the temporal asymmetry between the two input groups.
DS can be achieved by means of a single mechanism of STDP and synaptic depression.
STDP is sufficient to generate DS and to adapt the overall synaptic strength in a way that the postsynaptic cell becomes direction-selective and subthreshold for the non-prefered direction.
